chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Zurara, similar to it. Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, I heard him saying:
The divorced woman becomes irrevocably divorced at the first drop of blood in the final menstruation.
ai.seo_question: When does a revocable divorce become irrevocable in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the specific physiological marker for the termination of the waiting period (iddah) in a revocable divorce, anchoring the legal ruling in the natural cycle. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the 'final cycle' as the definitive boundary, ensuring that the transition from revocable to irrevocable status is tied to a clear, observable event. This precision prevents ambiguity in remarriage eligibility and reflects the practical application of Quranic injunctions on divorce.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara – similar to it’. Safwan, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara,from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying:
‘The divorced woman is irrevocably divorced during the first drop of the blood in the last menstruation’.
en.sarwar: 7. Safwan has narrated from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the foliowing: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
A woman divorced becomes stranger to him with the first drop of blood because of Hayd (menses) during the last Hayd (menses)-free period.’”
